name: The Verve
hook: A British band whose biggest song was built on an orchestral sample of a Rolling Stones song, and who lost its royalties for twenty years.
blurb: The Verve came from Wigan in the north of England, led by the singer Richard Ashcroft. Their 1997 song 'Bitter Sweet Symphony' is built on a looped string part taken from an orchestral version of the Rolling Stones' 1965 song 'The Last Time'. That version wasn't the Stones' own: it was produced by their former manager Andrew Loog Oldham, which is why the ownership was so tangled. The Verve had a licence for part of it, but the publisher, ABKCO, the company founded by the Stones' old manager Allen Klein, said they had used more than agreed and had the power to take the whole song. Ashcroft lost the songwriting credit and the royalties. It is rock's version of the Grand Upright case: a sample only partly cleared, and a band that signed away its rights. In 2019, in an agreement with ABKCO, Mick Jagger and Keith Richards gave the songwriting credit and the royalties back to him.
